we have developed a higher order continuum model for a one-dimensional crystal, derived the continuum limit of this model from the atomistic description, and demonstrated the convergence of the atomistic model to the continuum model by numerical simulations.
the higher order continuum models for crystals are more accurate than the Cauchy Born model, and that they can be derived rigorously from the atomistic description.
we have rigorously derived a fourth-order nonlinear elasticity model with periodic boundary condition for a chain with nearest neighbor interactions from its atomistic model.

a rigorous derivation of a higher order nonlinear continuum model in one dimension, from the atomistic model.
the rigorous derivation of higher order nonlinear elasticity models from atomistic descriptions and the a priori analysis of such models.
the rigorous mathematical analysis of the atomistic-to-continuum limits for nonlinear elastic models.

, the higher order model derived here is a more accurate continuum model than the Cauchy Born model for the one dimensional chain.

the higher-order nonlinear elasticity models can be used to describe the atomic-scale behavior of crystals, in the sense that the continuum solutions can be used to approximate the atomistic solutions with a high accuracy.

the higher order nonlinear elasticity models are derived from the atomistic models with the same order of accuracy as the atomistic models.

the higher order continuum models can be derived in an a priori fashion, without any need of fitting parameters.
, for higher order models, the atomistic description should be used as a benchmark for validating the continuum models.
